feedback:
Judged from earlier races and the candidate's contents only. This candidate is iteration 7's design (score 929.76, the best raced so far) with one change: base_speed 1.1 to 1.2. Everything else is unchanged: light body (mass 0.5, body_length 0.12), wheel_track 0.12, kp 4.5, ki 0.02, kd 1.0, sensors at y 0.08 with x spread of ±0.05, sensor_size 0.016, line_loss last_direction. All values are inside the contract ranges.

Evidence: iteration 7 finished 60/60 trials at base_speed 1.1 (oval 2.39 s, s-bend 2.44 s, slalom 2.63 s). Slalom max_error rose from 0.0215 at speed 1.0 (iteration 6) to 0.0233 at 1.1, about 0.002 per 0.1 of speed. That trend leaves room below the 0.06 m off-track limit at 1.2. Iteration 2 failed the slalom at speed 1.2, but on the heavier body with lower kd and sensors further back, so it is only weakly relevant. The expected gain is small, about 2 to 4 points, from roughly 0.1 s per track. The main risk is slalom off-track exits, which would cost far more than the gain. Approval is justified because the margin is adequate and the race will show the real effect of speed.

After the race, read slalom completion and max_error first, then completion_time. If slalom completion falls below 20/20, or slalom max_error passes about 0.03, the next design should return base_speed to 1.1, the best-supported value. Line_loss_events (one per run, worth up to about 100 points) have not moved under any gain, sensor or speed change, so the next gain or geometry test should not be spent on them unless the race shows when the loss occurs.
requested_changes: If slalom completion is below 20/20 or slalom max_error exceeds about 0.03, revert base_speed to 1.1, since iteration 7 finished 20/20 on all tracks at that speed.

If all tracks finish and completion_time drops by about 0.1 s per track with max_error stable, keep base_speed 1.2 and test kd 0.9 with kp 4.5, because steering_oscillation (0.17 to 0.27 in iterations 6 and 7) leaves room to reduce damping lag.

Do not change the sensor layout or line_loss on the next iteration: sensor y is at its maximum of 0.08, and the single line-loss event per run has not responded to any gain or geometry change in iterations 3 to 7.
